name: Jahdai
overview: Jahdai is a male figure from the tribe of Judah, identified uniquely as the son of Chelubai, also known as Caleb, according to 1 Chronicles 2:47. Beyond this genealogical note, Scripture provides limited additional information about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jahdai is a proper name meaning 'y-h-v-h lead,' reflecting a connection to the divine name of God, though it was not explicitly given by God. This name appears solely in 1 Chronicles 2:47.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records several inferred paternal relationships connected to Jahdai, including Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph, as mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2:47. These relationships suggest a family line but are not elaborated upon in detail.
scriptureSignificance: Jahdai's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical records of Judah, linking him to the lineage of Caleb. This connection situates him within the broader narrative of God's covenant people, underscoring the faithful heritage preserved in the tribe of Judah as recorded in the Old Testament.
